title: Bariatric Post-Op Meal Plan - Early Guidelines (Stage 1 & 2)
retired_reason: Retired 2025-06-01: Superseded by separate dedicated guides for Stage 1 (Liquids) and Stage 2 (Purees). Do not distribute.
summary: Legacy combined handout covering both Stage 1 clear liquids and Stage 2 purees. Discontinued due to patient confusion between fluid and pureed stages.

sections.heading: Early Post-Op Fluids
sections.content: Sip 1 ounce of water or broth every 15 minutes. Avoid drinking with meals.

sections.heading: Stage 2 Soft Purees
sections.content: Blend lean poultry, eggs, and beans with whole skim cow milk to achieve baby-food consistency. Strive for 50g protein daily.

title: Bariatric Post-Op Stage 2 Pureed Diet Handout (2024 Edition)
retired_reason: Superseded by DOC-BAR-002 v2: Protein targets updated from 50g to 60-80g; whole dairy removed due to high post-op lactose intolerance rates.
summary: 2024 version of Stage 2 Pureed guide. Outdated protein minimum and contained dairy recommendations that caused dumping/lactose cramping.

sections.heading: Stage 2 Pureed Principles
sections.content: At post-op week 2, begin pureed foods with the consistency of applesauce. Daily protein goal is 50g.

sections.heading: Dairy and Protein Shakes
sections.content: Mix standard skim milk with whey concentrate shakes. Dairy provides calcium and easy protein.

title: Bariatric Post-Op Stage 2 Pureed Nutrition Guide (Current 2025/2026)
summary: Current clinical protocol for Post-Op Week 2-3 bariatric patients transitioning to pureed foods. Includes mandatory lactose-free/plant-based protein options and strict 60-80g daily protein goal.

sections.heading: Stage 2 Pureed Criteria & Timing
sections.content: Post-Op Week 2 to 3 initiates Stage 2 (Pureed). All foods must be blended to a smooth applesauce or Greek yogurt consistency with no chunks, seeds, or skins.

sections.heading: Protein Target & Satiety (60g to 80g Daily)
sections.content: Target 60g to 80g of high biological value protein daily. Prioritize protein at every small meal (2 to 4 tablespoons per sitting).

sections.heading: Lactose Sensitivity & Plant / Whey Isolate Options
sections.content: Temporary secondary lactose intolerance is common after bariatric surgery (affects up to 40% of bypass and sleeve patients). Avoid regular cow milk. Use unsweetened almond milk, soy milk, pea protein broth, or 100% Whey Protein Isolate (WPI, <1g lactose). If gas, bloating, or diarrhea occurs, immediately discontinue whey concentrate and switch to hydrolyzed beef or pea-rice plant protein isolate.

sections.heading: Fluid Separation Rule
sections.content: Do NOT drink fluids with meals. Stop drinking 30 minutes before eating, and wait 30 minutes after eating before drinking. Drinking with meals washes pureed food through the pouch prematurely and triggers dumping syndrome.

sections.heading: Allowed Foods & Sample Day
sections.content: Allowed: pureed egg salad made with light mayo, silken tofu, blended low-fat cottage cheese (if tolerated), pureed chicken breast with chicken bone broth, pureed tuna with avocado. Avoid: rice, bread, corn, red meat purees.

title: Bariatric Post-Op Stage 1 Clear Liquids Protocol
summary: Comprehensive Stage 1 hydration and clear liquid protocol for days 1 to 7 post-bariatric surgery. Focuses on pouch healing, sipping technique, and sugar-free hydration.

sections.heading: Stage 1 Clear Liquids Protocol
sections.content: Days 1 to 7 post-surgery require strict clear liquids to protect staple lines. Consume a minimum of 48 to 64 oz of sugar-free, non-carbonated, decaffeinated fluids daily.

sections.heading: Approved Fluids
sections.content: Approved: Bone broth, diluted sugar-free electrolyte water, herbal decaf tea, clear protein water (e.g. Premier Protein Clear, Protein2o). Strictly avoid: red/purple dye liquids, carbonation, citrus juices, sugar.

sections.heading: Sipping Guidelines
sections.content: Sip 1 to 2 ounces over 15 to 20 minutes using a 1-oz medicine cup. Never use a straw because straws introduce air into the surgical pouch, causing severe pain and dilation.

title: Bariatric Post-Op Stage 3 Soft Foods Transition Guide
summary: Stage 3 guide covering the reintroduction of tender, fork-mashable soft proteins and steamed vegetables for weeks 4 through 6.

sections.heading: Stage 3 Soft Food Timing & Consistency
sections.content: Begins at Week 4 post-op after surgeon clearance. Foods must be tender and easily mashed with the back of a fork. Chew every bite 25 to 30 times.

sections.heading: Protein Goals & Suitable Sources
sections.content: Maintain 70g to 80g daily protein. Suitable sources: flaky white fish (tilapia, cod), ground turkey stewed in broth, scrambled eggs, well-cooked lentils, canned tuna in water.

title: Bariatric Micronutrient & Lifelong Vitamin Supplementation Protocol
summary: ASMBS guidelines for lifelong bariatric multivitamin, calcium citrate, iron, and vitamin B12 supplementation to prevent deficiency neuropathy and anemia.

sections.heading: ASMBS Recommended Supplement Regimen
sections.content: Post-bariatric anatomy requires lifelong supplementation. Take a high-potency bariatric specific multivitamin containing 200% daily value of vitamins A, D, E, K, zinc, and copper.

sections.heading: Calcium Citrate vs Calcium Carbonate
sections.content: Take 1,200mg to 1,500mg of Calcium Citrate daily in divided doses of 500mg. Calcium carbonate requires gastric stomach acid for absorption; bypass and sleeve patients do not produce sufficient acid. Calcium citrate absorbs independently of acid.

sections.heading: Iron and Calcium Separation Rule
sections.content: Never take calcium and iron at the same time. Calcium binds iron and inhibits its absorption. Separate iron supplements from calcium by at least 2 hours.

title: Bariatric Stage 4: Long-Term Stabilization & Solid Food Progression
summary: Long-term stabilization and solid food progression protocol starting at Month 3 post-op. Emphasizes solid protein satiety, fiber progression, and preventing weight regain.

sections.heading: Stage 4 Solid Protein Progression
sections.content: From Month 3 onward, transition to wholesome solid foods. Solid lean proteins (grilled chicken, sirloin, salmon) promote greater satiety than shakes or soft purees.

sections.heading: Pouch Rules for Long-Term Maintenance
sections.content: Always eat protein first, non-starchy vegetables second, and complex carbohydrates last. Stop eating at the very first sensation of fullness.

title: Gestational Diabetes Meal Planning: Strict Low-Carbohydrate Approach
summary: Intensive carbohydrate restriction handout for pregnant patients with refractory gestational diabetes. Caps lunch and dinner carbohydrates at 30g total carbs.

sections.heading: Breakfast Carbohydrate Ceiling
sections.content: Due to morning cortisol surges, keep breakfast carbohydrates under 15g. Consume eggs, avocado, and spinach. Avoid milk, cereal, and fruit before 11:00 AM.

sections.heading: Lunch and Dinner Carbohydrate Ceilings (Max 30g Net Carbs)
sections.content: To prevent postprandial spikes exceeding 120 mg/dL, strictly limit carbohydrates at lunch and dinner to no more than 30 grams of complex carbohydrates. Do not exceed 30g under any circumstances.

sections.heading: Ketone Monitoring Warning
sections.content: Test urine ketones every morning with Ketostix. Mild trace ketones are considered acceptable under this tight control regimen.

title: Gestational Diabetes Nutritional Care Guide: ADA & ACOG Standard Protocol
summary: ACOG and ADA consensus clinical guidelines for Gestational Diabetes. Mandates an individualized carbohydrate distribution across 3 meals and 2-3 snacks with an absolute minimum floor of 175g total carbohydrates daily (RDA in pregnancy) to protect fetal neurological development and prevent maternal starvation ketonuria without imposing rigid per-meal ceilings.

sections.heading: Fetal Brain Development & Minimum Daily Carbohydrates (175g Daily RDA)
sections.content: The developing fetal brain requires continuous maternal glucose oxidation. Pregnant individuals require a minimum of 175 grams of carbohydrate daily (RDA in pregnancy). Carbohydrate restriction below 175g induces maternal starvation ketosis and ketonuria, which are associated with compromised fetal neurodevelopmental outcomes. Strict carbohydrate restriction is clinically contraindicated.

sections.heading: Individualized Carbohydrate Distribution Across Meals & Snacks
sections.content: Rather than rigid per-meal gram mandates, carbohydrates should be distributed individually across meals and snacks based on personal blood glucose tolerance, postprandial patterns, physical activity, and medication timing. Focus on low-glycemic, fiber-rich complex carbohydrates (whole grains, legumes, vegetables) paired with quality protein and unsaturated fats.

sections.heading: Bedtime Snack Protocol to Prevent Overnight Ketonuria
sections.content: Always consume an individualized bedtime snack containing complex carbohydrates paired with protein (e.g., apple slices with peanut butter or Greek yogurt with seeds) to maintain stable nocturnal euglycemia and prevent morning starvation ketonuria.

title: Renal Diet Management: Potassium, Phosphorus, and Sodium Guidelines
summary: Outdated clinical guide for Stage 3-4 CKD patients managing serum potassium and phosphorus. Review date expired in January 2024 (overdue for clinical review).

sections.heading: Potassium Restriction Protocol
sections.content: Limit daily potassium to under 2,000 mg. Avoid bananas, potatoes, oranges, tomatoes, and avocados. Double-boil root vegetables to leach potassium.

sections.heading: Phosphorus Additives & Protein Targets
sections.content: Keep protein intake moderate at 0.6g to 0.8g per kg body weight. Strictly avoid foods containing inorganic phosphate additives (pyrophosphate, sodium hexametaphosphate).

title: Legacy Very-Low-Calorie Diet (VLCD) 800-Calorie Rapid Loss Protocol
retired_reason: Retired by Clinical Director: VLCD 800kcal protocol discontinued due to gallstone risk, electrolyte shifts, and high weight regain rebound. Practice transitioned to GLP-1 nutritional therapy and moderate caloric deficits.
summary: Retired 800-calorie liquid meal replacement protocol. Kept for clinical record reference only. MUST NOT BE DISTRIBUTED TO PATIENTS.

sections.heading: VLCD 800-Calorie Daily Regimen (DISCONTINUED)
sections.content: Four medical meal-replacement shakes daily providing 800 kcal and 80g protein total. No solid food permitted during induction.

sections.heading: Clinical Contraindications & Risks
sections.content: High risk of cholelithiasis (gallstones), cardiac arrhythmia, and severe lean mass wasting. Discontinued practice-wide.

title: Type 2 Diabetes Carbohydrate Counting & Plate Method Handout (2023 Edition)
retired_reason: Superseded by DOC-DM-001 v2: Updated with current ADA Standards of Care, glycemic variability, and CGM metric interpretation.
summary: Old edition of diabetes plate method. Lacked continuous glucose monitoring guidance and modern plant-based protein substitutes.

sections.heading: The Diabetes Plate Method
sections.content: Fill 1/2 of your 9-inch plate with non-starchy vegetables, 1/4 with lean protein, and 1/4 with carbohydrate foods.

title: Type 2 Diabetes Blood Sugar & Balanced Plate Guide (Current 2025/2026)
summary: Current comprehensive guide for Type 2 Diabetes self-management. Details the Diabetes Plate Method, fiber pairing, postprandial glucose goals (<180 mg/dL), and time-in-range optimization.

sections.heading: The Diabetes Plate Method: Visual Portioning
sections.content: Use a 9-inch dinner plate: Fill 1/2 with non-starchy vegetables (broccoli, salad greens, peppers, cauliflower), fill 1/4 with lean protein (skinless poultry, tofu, eggs, beans, fish), and fill 1/4 with whole grain complex carbohydrates (quinoa, brown rice, sweet potato).

sections.heading: Carbohydrate Quality & The Fiber Cushion Rule
sections.content: Pair all carbohydrate foods with dietary fiber and healthy fats or proteins. Strive for at least 30g to 35g of fiber daily. Fiber slows carbohydrate hydrolysis and blunts postprandial glucose spikes.

sections.heading: Target Blood Glucose Ranges
sections.content: ADA clinical targets: Fasting/pre-meal blood sugar between 80 and 130 mg/dL. Two hours post-meal blood sugar below 180 mg/dL.

title: Hypoglycemia Emergency Action Guide: The Rule of 15
summary: Emergency clinical handout explaining acute hypoglycemia management for patients on insulin or sulfonylureas using the standardized Rule of 15.
synonyms: client got shaky and her sugar was low after insulin
shaky and sugar low after insulin

sections.heading: Hypoglycemia Signs & Definition (Glucose < 70 mg/dL)
sections.content: Hypoglycemia is blood glucose under 70 mg/dL. Symptoms include shakiness, diaphoresis (sweating), tachycardia (racing heart), confusion, dizziness, and irritability.

sections.heading: The Rule of 15 Treatment Step-by-Step
sections.content: Step 1: Ingest 15 grams of fast-acting simple carbohydrates (4 glucose tablets, 1/2 cup fruit juice or regular soda, or 1 tube glucose gel). Step 2: Wait 15 minutes and re-test blood sugar. Step 3: If still under 70 mg/dL, repeat with another 15g of fast carbs. Step 4: Once glucose is above 70 mg/dL, eat a snack with protein and complex carbs.

sections.heading: Critical Warning: Glucagon Emergency
sections.content: If the individual becomes unconscious or cannot swallow, do NOT place anything in their mouth. Administer nasal or injectable emergency glucagon immediately and call 911.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) Patient Quick-Start & Trend Guide
condition: Dexcom G7 / Freestyle Libre 3 CGM Users
summary: Patient education guide for interpreting continuous glucose monitor trend arrows, understanding lag time between interstitial fluid and capillary blood, and avoiding over-treating highs.

sections.heading: Sensor Lag Time: Interstitial vs Blood Glucose
sections.content: CGM sensors measure glucose in interstitial fluid under the skin, which lags fingerstick blood glucose by 5 to 10 minutes. If symptoms do not match sensor readings, always verify with a fingerstick meter.

sections.heading: Interpreting Trend Arrows & Preventing Stacking
sections.content: A straight arrow means glucose is stable (changing <1 mg/dL per minute). An angled upward arrow means rising 1-2 mg/dL/min. A double straight up arrow means rising rapidly (>2 mg/dL/min). Do not stack insulin boluses or skip meals based on rapid swings.

title: GLP-1 Agonist Nutrition Companion (Semaglutide / Tirzepatide Guide)
summary: Clinical nutrition guide for patients prescribed GLP-1 receptor agonists. Covers lean muscle preservation, hydration, nausea mitigation, and preventing constipation and delayed gastric emptying complications.

sections.heading: Preserving Lean Skeletal Muscle (1.2g to 1.5g Protein/kg)
sections.content: Rapid weight loss on GLP-1 medications risks significant lean muscle mass loss (up to 40% of total weight lost). Patients must consume a minimum of 1.2g to 1.5g of dietary protein per kilogram of ideal body weight daily. Supplement with resistance training twice weekly.

sections.heading: Nausea & Early Satiety Management Strategies
sections.content: Because GLP-1 agonists delay gastric emptying, large meals cause intense nausea, reflux, and vomiting. Eat 4 to 5 small meals throughout the day. Stop eating the moment you feel satisfied. Avoid high-fat, greasy, or deep-fried foods, which sit in the stomach for hours.

sections.heading: Hydration and Electrolyte Goals
sections.content: Blunted thirst cues are common. Drink a minimum of 64 to 80 oz of water daily. Include one serving of low-sugar electrolyte replenishment to prevent dizziness and hypovolemia.

sections.heading: Constipation Prevention Protocol
sections.content: Delayed peristalsis can lead to severe constipation. Incorporate 2 tablespoons of ground chia or flaxseed daily, kiwi fruit, and adequate water. If no bowel movement for 48 hours, begin osmotic magnesium citrate or polyethylene glycol.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Mediterranean Meal Planner
summary: Evidence-based Mediterranean dietary framework emphasizing polyphenol-rich olive oil, omega-3 fatty acids, legumes, and cruciferous vegetables for metabolic syndrome.

sections.heading: Core Pillars of Mediterranean Nutrition
sections.content: Base all meals around extra virgin olive oil (2 tablespoons daily), leafy greens, whole grains, and legumes. Consume wild fatty fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel) at least 2 times per week.

sections.heading: Limiting Pro-Inflammatory Foods
sections.content: Minimize ultra-processed foods, refined seed oils, added sugars, and processed delicatessen meats.

title: PCOS Insulin Resistance & Hormone Balancing Nutrition Guide
summary: Targeted nutrition protocol for PCOS focusing on hyperinsulinemia, lowering androgen levels, inositol supplementation, and stabilizing ovarian hormone production.

sections.heading: The Insulin-Androgen Link in PCOS
sections.content: Elevated insulin drives ovarian theca cells to overproduce testosterone, causing irregular cycles, hirsutism, and cystic acne. Stabilizing blood sugar is the primary clinical therapy to restore ovulatory regularity.

sections.heading: Low-Glycemic Meal Construction
sections.content: Combine high-fiber complex carbs with healthy fats and protein. Avoid naked carbohydrates on an empty stomach.

sections.heading: Myo-Inositol & D-Chiro-Inositol Support
sections.content: Research supports a 40:1 ratio of Myo-Inositol to D-Chiro-Inositol (2,000mg twice daily) to improve cellular insulin receptor sensitivity and promote spontaneous ovulation.

title: Peri-Menopause & Post-Menopause Bone Density & Sarcopenia Nutrition Plan
summary: Nutritional strategy for perimenopausal and postmenopausal women combating accelerated bone demineralization, visceral adiposity redistribution, and sarcopenia.

sections.heading: Combatting Estrogen-Deficient Bone Resorption
sections.content: Declining estradiol accelerates osteoclast activity, resulting in up to 10% bone mineral loss during the 5 years surrounding final menstrual period. Target 1,200mg calcium daily from bioavailable dietary sources (fortified dairy, sardines, leafy greens).

sections.heading: Combating Sarcopenia: The Leucine Threshold
sections.content: Post-menopausal muscle requires 2.5g to 3g of leucine per meal to trigger muscle protein synthesis (e.g., 30g to 35g of complete protein per feeding window).

title: Low-FODMAP Diet Phase 1: Strict Elimination Protocol (2-6 Weeks)
summary: Monash University validated protocol for Phase 1 strict FODMAP elimination. Designed to resolve visceral bloating, gas, abdominal pain, and erratic bowel habits within 2 to 6 weeks.

sections.heading: Phase 1 Elimination Purpose & Duration
sections.content: Phase 1 is a diagnostic test, NOT a permanent diet. Strictly eliminate all high-FODMAP foods for 2 to 6 weeks until GI symptoms improve by at least 70%.

sections.heading: High-FODMAP Foods to Strictly Avoid
sections.content: Avoid: Garlic and onions (including garlic powder), wheat/rye in large quantities, apples, pears, watermelon, honey, high-fructose corn syrup, milk, yogurt, beans, lentils, cauliflower, and mushrooms.

sections.heading: Safe Low-FODMAP Alternatives
sections.content: Safe: Garlic-infused olive oil (fructans are water-soluble, not fat-soluble), green tops of scallions/spring onions, sourdough spelt bread, blueberries, strawberries, carrots, spinach, potatoes, firm tofu, eggs, and all plain meats.

title: Low-FODMAP Diet Phase 2: Systematic Challenge & Reintroduction Protocol
summary: Step-by-step reintroduction protocol to test specific FODMAP subgroups (fructose, sorbitol, mannitol, lactose, fructans, GOS) one at a time over 3 days.

sections.heading: Systematic 3-Day Challenge Protocol
sections.content: Test one FODMAP group at a time over 3 consecutive days in increasing portions (e.g., Day 1: 1/4 clove garlic; Day 2: 1/2 clove; Day 3: 1 whole clove). Record symptoms for 48 hours following day 3.

sections.heading: Washout Periods Between Challenges
sections.content: Always institute a 3-day washout period returning to strict Low-FODMAP eating between different test categories to prevent symptom carryover.

title: DASH Diet & Sodium Reduction Guide for Hypertension
summary: Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) protocol detailing 1,500mg - 2,300mg sodium targets, potassium-magnesium balance, and label reading for hidden sodium.

sections.heading: Sodium Ceiling & Reading Nutrition Labels
sections.content: Target 1,500mg to 2,300mg sodium per day. More than 70% of dietary sodium comes from restaurant meals and packaged goods. Aim for under 140mg sodium per serving for a low-sodium food.

sections.heading: Electrolyte Synergy: Potassium, Magnesium, and Calcium
sections.content: Sodium excretion is promoted by dietary potassium and magnesium. Consume leafy greens, beans, Greek yogurt, and seeds daily.

title: Clinical Escalation Protocol: Suspected Eating Disorder / Severe Restriction
condition: Anorexia Nervosa, Bulimia Nervosa, ARFID, OSFED
summary: INTERNAL CLINICAL PROTOCOL ONLY. Mandatory clinical red-flag triggers, SCOFF screening criteria, lab escalation markers, and referral workflow for patients showing eating disorder pathology.

sections.heading: Mandatory Practice Red Flags (Clinical Stop Rule)
sections.content: If a patient presents with BMI < 16.5, heart rate < 45 bpm, systolic BP < 85 mmHg, serum potassium < 3.2 mEq/L, or active purging > 3x weekly, outpatient dietitian care is suspended. Dietitian must immediately escalate to Dr. Jenkins and initiate emergency psychiatric/medical co-management.

sections.heading: Internal Communication & Patient Handout Prohibition
sections.content: THIS DOCUMENT IS AN INTERNAL CLINICAL PROTOCOL AND MUST NEVER BE DISTRIBUTED TO PATIENTS. Do NOT provide caloric counting sheets or restrictive meal plans to patients screening positive on the SCOFF inventory.

title: Practice Standard Operating Procedure: Insurance Superbills & MNT Billing Codes
summary: INTERNAL STAFF BILLING GUIDE. Details CPT codes 97802 (initial MNT, 15 min), 97803 (follow-up MNT), G0270, ICD-10 crosswalks, and Medicare Part B qualifying criteria.

sections.heading: CPT 97802 & 97803 Units & Documentation Rules
sections.content: CPT 97802 is billed in 15-minute increments for the initial assessment. Minimum time for 1 unit is 8 minutes; 2 units = 23-37 minutes; 3 units = 38-52 minutes; 4 units = 53-67 minutes. CPT 97803 is billed for re-assessment visits.

sections.heading: Medicare Part B Coverage Limitations
sections.content: Medicare Part B ONLY covers Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) for Diabetes (Type 1, Type 2, Gestational) and Renal Disease (non-dialysis stages). Obesity alone without diabetes is NOT covered under Medicare Part B.

title: Clinical Policy: Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) Sensor Billing & CPT 95249/95250
summary: INTERNAL CLINICAL POLICY. Practice guidelines for clinical sensor placement (CPT 95249), 72-hour retrospective CGM diagnostic study (CPT 95250), and physician interpretation crosswalks.

sections.heading: CPT 95249 Placement Workflow
sections.content: Billed once per sensor initiation. Requires clinical documentation of sensor warm-up, calibration, patient mobile pairing, and skin prep using Cavilon wipes.

title: Draft Protocol: Micro-Dosing Plant Protein in Chronic Renal Failure
summary: UNAPPROVED DRAFT. Investigational handout exploring keto-analogue supplemented very low protein diet (VLPD) for pre-dialysis renal patients. Under active review by Medical Advisory Board.
synonyms: plant protein in kidney disease draft

sections.heading: Investigational Keto-Analogue Dosing
sections.content: DRAFT CONTENT: Restricting protein to 0.3g/kg while supplementing essential amino acid keto-analogues may delay dialysis initiation.

title: Guía del Método del Plato y Control de Glucosa para Diabetes Tipo 2
summary: Versión oficial en español: Guía del autocontrol de la diabetes tipo 2 con el método del plato de 9 pulgadas, porciones visuales, conteo de carbohidratos complejos y metas de glucosa en sangre.

sections.heading: El Método del Plato de 9 Pulgadas
sections.content: Use un plato estándar de 9 pulgadas: Llene 1/2 con vegetales sin almidón (espinacas, nopales, pimientos, chayote, brócoli), 1/4 con proteínas magras (pollo sin piel, pescado, huevos, frijoles negros), y 1/4 con carbohidratos complejos (tortillas de maíz nixtamalizado, arroz integral, frijoles).

sections.heading: Calidad de Carbohidratos y Fibra Dietética
sections.content: Consuma un mínimo de 30g a 35g de fibra al día. Acompañe los carbohidratos con grasas saludables o proteínas magras para reducir la velocidad de absorción y evitar hiperglucemias postprandiales.

sections.heading: Metas Clínicas de Glucosa en Sangre
sections.content: Metas según la Asociación Americana de Diabetes (ADA): En ayunas y antes de comer entre 80 y 130 mg/dL. Dos horas después de una comida: menos de 180 mg/dL.

title: Type 1 Diabetes & Insulin Pump Patient Essentials
summary: Comprehensive foundational guide for patients with Type 1 Diabetes initiating automated insulin delivery (AID) pumps, basal vs bolus insulin principles, carb factor ratios, and active insulin time.

sections.heading: Basal Insulin vs Bolus Insulin Ratios
sections.content: Basal insulin covers background metabolic glucose output while sleeping and fasting (roughly 40-50% of total daily dose). Bolus insulin covers mealtime carbohydrates (carb-to-insulin ratio) and corrects elevated blood glucose spikes (correction factor/insulin sensitivity factor).

sections.heading: Insulin-to-Carbohydrate Ratio (ICR) Basics
sections.content: Your endocrinologist or RD calculates your personal ICR (e.g., 1 unit per 10g or 15g carbs). Always enter accurate carbohydrate counts into the pump bolus wizard before meals.

sections.heading: Active Insulin Time & Avoiding Stacking
sections.content: Bolus insulin analogues (Lispro, Aspart) have an active insulin time (insulin on board, IOB) of 3 to 4 hours. Never deliver manual correction boluses less than 2 hours apart, as insulin stacking causes severe delayed hypoglycemia.

title: Diabetes Sick-Day Management Protocol: Hydration, Ketones & Blood Sugar Rules
summary: Emergency and acute illness guidelines for patients with diabetes. Covers hourly hydration, mandatory ketone testing when glucose >250 mg/dL, continuing baseline insulin even when not eating, holding SGLT2 inhibitors (Jardiance, Farxiga), and urgent ER triage criteria.
synonyms: patient on jardiance has the flu and is not eating

sections.heading: SGLT2 Inhibitor (Jardiance, Farxiga) Sick-Day Hold Rule
sections.content: Temporarily discontinue SGLT2 inhibitors (such as Jardiance / empagliflozin or Farxiga / dapagliflozin) immediately if you contract the flu, an acute illness, fever, or are not eating / vomiting. Continuing SGLT2 inhibitors while sick or dehydrated carries a high risk of euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (euDKA), where dangerous ketoacidosis develops even with near-normal blood glucose levels. Resume only once eating normally and fully hydrated under clinician guidance.

sections.heading: Never Discontinue Insulin During Illness
sections.content: Never stop taking basal insulin during acute sickness, vomiting, or infection, even if you are unable to eat. Infection increases cortisol and epinephrine counter-regulatory hormones, sharply raising insulin requirements. Stopping basal insulin causes rapid onset Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA).

sections.heading: Blood Glucose & Ketone Monitoring Frequency
sections.content: Check blood glucose every 2 to 4 hours. Test urine or blood ketones every 4 hours whenever blood glucose exceeds 250 mg/dL or if nausea, abdominal pain, or shortness of breath occurs.

sections.heading: Sick-Day Hydration & Electrolytes
sections.content: Sip 8 ounces of fluid every hour while awake. If blood glucose is above 200 mg/dL, drink sugar-free electrolyte broths and water. If blood glucose drops below 150 mg/dL and you cannot hold down solid meals, switch to sip fluids with simple carbohydrates (diluted juice, sports drinks, gelatin) to provide 15g carbs per hour.

sections.heading: When to Call the Clinician or Go to the Emergency Department
sections.content: Seek immediate emergency hospital medical evaluation if: (1) Moderate-to-large ketones persist for >4 hours; (2) Inability to keep fluids down for >4 hours; (3) Repeated vomiting; (4) Persistent fever >101.5°F; or (5) Fruity breath or labored breathing.

title: Prediabetes Reversal Guide: Nutrition, Weight Reduction & Insulin Sensitivity
summary: Evidence-based National Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) guide for reversing insulin resistance and preventing progression to Type 2 Diabetes through 7% weight loss and Mediterranean-style eating.

sections.heading: The Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) Evidence Target
sections.content: Clinical trials prove that achieving a 7% to 10% reduction in body weight combined with 150 minutes of weekly moderate physical activity reduces the risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes by 58% (71% in adults aged 60+).

sections.heading: Reversing Insulin Resistance via Carbohydrate Quality
sections.content: Replace refined grains (white flour, white rice, sweetened cereals) with high-viscosity soluble fibers (chia seeds, oats, legumes, barley). Avoid sugar-sweetened beverages entirely.

sections.heading: Physical Activity & Post-Meal Muscle Glucose Uptake
sections.content: Skeletal muscle absorbs glucose independently of insulin during contraction. A brisk 15-minute walk immediately following your largest meal significantly attenuates postprandial glycemic excursions.

title: Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Dual Glucose & Renal Protein Care Guide
condition: Type 2 Diabetes with Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 1-3
summary: Joint ADA/KDIGO consensus clinical education for diabetic kidney disease: moderate protein target (0.8g/kg/day), sodium limitation (<2,300 mg), blood pressure control (<130/80), and SGLT2i/GLP-1 renal protective considerations.

sections.heading: Joint ADA/KDIGO Protein Target (0.8g per kg Body Weight)
sections.content: For patients with non-dialysis diabetic kidney disease, the consensus ADA and KDIGO dietary protein recommendation is exactly 0.8g per kilogram body weight per day. Excess protein intake (>1.3g/kg) increases intraglomerular pressure and accelerates diabetic glomerulosclerosis.

sections.heading: Sodium Restriction & Blood Pressure Targets
sections.content: Restrict dietary sodium to under 2,000 to 2,300 mg daily to enhance the antiproteinuric effects of RAAS inhibitors (ACE/ARBs). Target blood pressure is <130/80 mmHg.

sections.heading: Hypoglycemia Risk as Kidney Function Declines
sections.content: The kidneys clear 30-40% of circulating insulin. As eGFR drops, insulin clearance decreases and circulating half-life lengthens, sharply increasing the risk of prolonged, severe hypoglycemia. Frequent glucose monitoring is essential.

title: Clinical Escalation Protocol: Outpatient Nutrition Red Flags & Emergency Triage
condition: Urgent Clinical Red Flags & Emergency Escalation
summary: INTERNAL PRACTICE SOP. Mandatory emergency triage and urgent clinical escalation guidelines for outpatient dietitians. Covers SGLT2 inhibitor euglycemic DKA, intractable vomiting, severe hypoglycemia, T1D ketosis, eating disorder purging/restriction, and hyperkalemia.

sections.heading: SGLT2 Inhibitor Euglycemic DKA Red Flag Protocol
sections.content: Patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors (Jardiance/empagliflozin, Farxiga/dapagliflozin, Invokana/canagliflozin, Steglatro/ertugliflozin) who experience acute illness, infection, vomiting, anorexia, or carbohydrate restriction are at life-threatening risk for Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (euDKA) with normal or mildly elevated blood glucose (< 200 mg/dL). MANDATORY ACTIONS: 1) Instruct patient/caregiver to HOLD the SGLT2 inhibitor immediately. 2) Check blood or urine ketones immediately. 3) If ketones are positive, persistent vomiting occurs, or patient cannot maintain hydration, direct immediately to the Emergency Department or Urgent Care. Routine sick-day meal guides are secondary and NEVER a substitute for medical escalation.

sections.heading: Intractable Vomiting & Dehydration Red Flag
sections.content: Bariatric surgery patients (any post-op stage) or patients on GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists experiencing persistent vomiting (> 24-48 hours) or inability to keep water/fluids down are at acute risk of Wernicke's encephalopathy, anastomotic stricture, severe electrolyte depletion, and acute kidney injury. MANDATORY ACTIONS: Escalate immediately to bariatric surgeon or emergency department. Do NOT advise oral fluid rehydration without emergency clearance.

sections.heading: Severe Hypoglycemia Emergency Protocol
sections.content: Severe hypoglycemia characterized by unconsciousness, seizure, combative behavior, or inability to safely swallow cannot be treated with oral 15-15 carbohydrates. MANDATORY ACTIONS: Administer prescribed emergency glucagon (nasal Baqsimi or injectable Gvoke/Glucagen) immediately. Call 911. Do not place food or fluids in the mouth.

sections.heading: Type 1 Diabetes Sick-Day & Ketone Escalation
sections.content: T1D patients with elevated blood sugar (> 240 mg/dL) and moderate-to-large ketones require immediate physician/endocrinologist contact for supplemental rapid-acting correction per their management plan. NEVER advise skipping or holding basal insulin during illness.

sections.heading: Eating Disorder Safety & Purging Red Flag
sections.content: Patients exhibiting active purging (vomiting, laxative/diuretic misuse), extreme caloric restriction, or meal skipping alongside a weight-loss request must NOT receive weight-loss, fasting, or hypocaloric meal plans. Dietitians must place a safety hold and initiate multidisciplinary referral (mental health + primary care physician).

sections.heading: CKD Hyperkalemia Emergency Protocol
sections.content: Serum potassium > 5.0 mEq/L (critical >= 6.0 mEq/L) carries severe cardiac arrhythmia risk. Immediately review lab collection date, instruct patient to hold high-potassium supplements/substitutes, and urgently notify the nephrologist or PCP.

sections.heading: Prescriber Medication Scope Boundary
sections.content: Outpatient dietitians do NOT prescribe or alter medication doses, insulin pump basal rates, or drug regimens. Requests to change medication doses (e.g., cutting metformin for GI upset, adjusting basal insulin) must be referred directly to the prescribing provider.
